results.exact_unused_slice: A visuo-tactile world model that learns the artisan's fingertip judgment of WHEN a kneaded incense (nerikoh) paste has reached the correct consistency for that day's temperature/humidity, deciding incrementally how much honey/water/plum to add — i.e. closed-loop adaptation of a moisture-target to ambient climate during kneading, plus the downstream maturation-readiness judgment. No work pairs visuo-tactile/world-model methods with this honey-binder consistency-for-climate decision, nor with kneaded-incense maturation.
results.honest_adjacency: Both axes are touched. Technique family (visuo-tactile dynamics prediction / world models for deformables, and visuo-tactile material-softness estimation) is well established (VIRDO++ 2210.03701; Deep Visuo-Tactile Learning). The sibling domain of kneadable paste is directly addressed by robotic dough manipulation and elasto-plastic shaping (Robotic Dough Shaping 2208.00386; Elasto-Plastic Shaping w/ MBRL 2107.06924; stretchable tactile array kneading dough PMC11535439). What is missing is the incense-specific, climate-conditioned, by-feel consistency target and maturation judgment.
results.reasoning: After 5 reformulations the application 'nerikoh consistency-by-feel for temp/humidity' returns only how-to artisan guides (KyaraZen, incensemaking.com) with zero AI/robotics, but the technique family and the sibling kneadable-paste domain (dough/plasticine/clay) are richly covered by robot tactile/world-model manipulation work, including explicit dough-kneading. Adjacency exists on both axes, so this is NARROW, not OPEN. It is not CLOSED because no work targets paste-consistency-to-climate or incense maturation.

prior_art_found.snippet: an AI-mediated olfactory interaction system that reinterprets the traditional Japanese incense game Genji-ko as a collaborative human-AI sensory experience ... The AI co-smelling partner integrates olfactory sensing hardware, a scent classification model, and an LLM-based conversational interface ... The model uses a Transformer encoder backbone coupled with an MLP classifier head for 5-class incense categorization. ... Genji-ko is a social olfactory game ... participants compare sequences of five incense scents.
prior_art_found.relation: NEAR-DIRECT adjacency on the APPLICATION axis: AI making the comparative scent-discernment judgment of a traditional Japanese incense game (Genji-ko, a sibling of kumiko-ko) via a learned scent classifier. This is essentially 'AI plays the incense-identification game', the same capability the C4 gap describes, though it classifies incense from live olfactory-sensor data, not from agarwood volatile/molecular profiles.

results.exact_unused_slice: Mapping agarwood VOLATILE/MOLECULAR profiles (e.g. 2-(2-phenylethyl)chromones, sesquiterpenes) to the kodo rikkoku-gomi identity judgment — i.e. predicting 'which of the six classical jinkoh types/origins (Kyara, Rakoku, Manaka, Manaban, Sasora, Sumotara) is this sample' as the kumiko game decides — from chemistry, using a structure/QSOR-style or volatile-profile model. Adjacent work either (a) classifies agarwood by quality GRADE (KNN/OPLS/e-nose), not by the named rikkoku identity, or (b) plays the incense game with AI but classifies from live olfactory-sensor signals (Smell with Genji), not from molecular/volatile chemistry. No work joins molecular/volatile-profile odor ML to the rikkoku identify-this-wood discernment judgment.
results.honest_adjacency: Both axes are heavily touched. APPLICATION axis: agarwood is already classified/graded by ML, e-nose, and GC-MS chemometrics (PMC3292139; KNN on GC-MS; OPLS class models), AND the kodo incense-identification GAME itself is already AI-mediated via a Transformer scent classifier in 'Smell with Genji' (arXiv 2602.02785, CHI 2026). TECHNIQUE axis: molecular-structure-to-odor ML (including woody-note QSOR, Morgan-fingerprint XGBoost) is mature. The combination is therefore strongly bracketed; only the specific chemistry-to-rikkoku-identity link is unfilled.
results.reasoning: Five reformulations surfaced dense prior art on both axes. The application (machine discrimination of agarwood/jinkoh) is well covered by e-nose and GC-MS+chemometrics, and crucially the kumiko-style incense-discernment game is already done with AI ('Smell with Genji', 2602.02785), which is a near-direct hit on the gap's framing. The technique (molecular-structure odor prediction) is also mature. This is comfortably NARROW. Not CLOSED only because no single work maps molecular/volatile agarwood chemistry to the rikkoku-gomi named-identity judgment; existing agarwood ML targets quality grade, and the game-playing AI classifies from sensor signals rather than chemistry.
